children: Chile's central bank held its benchmark interest rate at 4.5% on Tuesday, in line with analysts' expectations.
The unanimous decision marked the bank's sixth consecutive pause.
With the economic outlook clouded by unusual uncertainty, the board said it is evaluating scenarios where unexpected shifts in inflation could require adjustments to monetary policy.
Annual inflation accelerated in August to 4.1% from 3.5% in July, moving outside the central bank's tolerance range of 3%, plus or minus one percentage point.
Last month, the central bank reported that Chile's economy shrank 0.2% year-on-year in the second quarter, missing expectations as weaker copper output weighed on the country's crucial mining sector.
While the domestic economy is expected to pick up pace toward 2027, there is a risk that its current weakness may prove more persistent than previously forecast, the bank said.
The future path of interest rates will be assessed on a meeting-by-meeting basis, the central bank added.
